name: Week 28 Optional KB — Outside Snatch Flow + Brutal Complex
description: **Optional and deliberately short.** Run it whenever a window opens after the three gym sessions; it is not tied to a weekday and missing it does not make the week incomplete. Outside Snatch Flow remains the conditioning anchor, and the Brutal Complex stays at 35 with rounds—not load—as the variable.

dayOverview.theme: A deliberately short KB day with sleep deprivation in mind. We keep the Outside Snatch Flow as the conditioning anchor and the Brutal Complex as the strength finisher, but reduce volume to fit a constrained window. The focus is on maintaining form and staying consistent rather than chasing load or rounds.

spotlights.why: The ab-stance squats and close-grip pushups are what make the Brutal Complex brutal — the swing and row are rest. This beat has a technique ceiling that rewards stability over load, perfect for a short, tired session.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W28 gives the Outside Snatch Flow and Brutal Complex a short repeat. Rotate again next week instead of letting this pairing become permanent.
watchpoints:
**🌀 Brutal Complex at 35. Not a range — 35.** swing → ab-stance goblet squat → alternating bent-over row → close-grip pushup on the bell handles. Circuit-style, ~10-12 reps per move, ~45s between rounds (reduced for short session).

**Rounds are the variable, not the bell.** Two rounds is the target for this short session; go to three only if feeling strong. **Stop a round when the hinge stops holding** — there's a bent-over row and loaded squats in there, and a broken hinge under fatigue is where this block would hurt you.
**🔆 Close-grip pushup on the bell: elbows TUCKED, shoulders packed DOWN, ribs down** 🛑. This is the beat with a technique ceiling — focus on quality, not quantity.
**Pacing map (your read, and it's right): the squats and the pushups are the work. The swing and the row are the rest.** Spend your effort accordingly on a short day.

**🌀 Outside Snatch Flow — light bell, 2 rounds each side (reduced from 2-3).** The spotlight rotates off; it's a known chain now. The outside-arc snatch reads as core, not shoulder — 35 ran fine for extra rounds when fresh, but today we keep it to two rounds each side.

figure-8 → tactical clean → transverse lunge → outside snatch → windmill → snatch → thruster → deep squat press → hand-to-hand swing.

- **The outside snatch is a CORE move**, which is what you found last time — the bell traveling off the midline makes it anti-rotation work, not shoulder work. Let the trunk resist the pull rather than muscling the arc
- **Punch the hand through** so the bell rolls onto the forearm instead of banging it
- **Pack the shoulder DOWN at every catch** 🛑
- **The chain shouldn't have stops in it** — you know the order now, so spend the attention on the transitions
**KB curl, LEFT FIRST** 🔥, light bell. Same as Tuesday — this is the frequency, not the intensity.

**Strict overhead press holds 50 — with a 2-3s PAUSE AT LOCKOUT every rep** 🛑. 50 is the Arrilaga ceiling and it read "pretty easy" Tuesday, so the pause is the progression, not the bell. KB row holds 50 — maintenance.
**Intensity tags:** 🔥 near-failure OK — KB curl (last set only). 🛑 keep it shy — snatch, overhead press, bent press, windmill, the close-grip pushup.
**Banded shoulder prep + protective shrug stay in the warm-up.**
**Sleep deprivation watch:** If feeling unusually fatigued, reduce the Outside Snatch Flow to one round each side and the Brutal Complex to one round. Prioritize form over completion.

sets.name: Warm-Up (incl. Bottoms-Up Cuff Prep + Figure-8 Passes)
sets.notes: Light bell throughout. The figure-8 passes here are the coordination primer — the heavy version lives on Tuesday.

exercises.notes: Slow, close to the head. Shoulders packed down.
Light bell inverted. Cuff prep and grip — and it rehearses the exact packed-down lockout the press block is about to ask for.
**Light bell** — this is the coordination primer, not the 50lb Tuesday finisher. Hinge, don't squat.
Hinged slightly forward, tight fists, thumbs tucked.
Protective activation. Down and back at the top.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~3 min)
sets.notes: 1 round of all 7 banded moves (~3 min). Sustained tension, no rest between positions.

sets.name: 🌀 Outside Snatch Flow — the Keeper (Short)
sets.notes:
**Single light bell (~25-35lb), 2 rounds each side (reduced for short session).**

figure-8 → tactical clean → transverse lunge → outside snatch → windmill → snatch → thruster → deep squat press → hand-to-hand swing.

- **The outside snatch is a CORE move**, which is what you found last time — the bell traveling off the midline makes it anti-rotation work, not shoulder work. Let the trunk resist the pull rather than muscling the arc
- **Punch the hand through** so the bell rolls onto the forearm instead of banging it
- **Pack the shoulder DOWN at every catch** 🛑
- **The chain shouldn't have stops in it** — you know the order now, so spend the attention on the transitions

**Short session note:** Keep the bell light and the transitions smooth. If feeling fatigued, reduce to one round each side.

sets.name: Strength — Row + Strict Press + KB Curl (Between the Big Blocks) 🛑
sets.notes: One maintenance round between the flow and complex. This preserves the known strength work without turning the optional session into another long gym day.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50. Hinged, flat back, bell to the hip.
- **Pack the shoulder DOWN and BACK** before the elbow moves
- **Elbow drives past the ribs**, not flared wide
- Slow return, full stretch at the bottom

**LOAD:** 50 across all sets — strict, clean to rack, press straight up, NO push-press. **50 is the ceiling here, so the pause is the progression.**
- **2-3s PAUSE AT LOCKOUT on every rep** — bicep by the ear, shoulder packed DOWN, ribs down, and hold it. Either the position survives three seconds or it doesn't; there's no way to fudge it
- **Strict, ribs DOWN**, no rib flare
- Full lockout before the pause starts — don't start counting from a soft elbow
- Both sides to the same standard

It read *"pretty easy"* on Tuesday at this same 50. The pause is what makes it hard again without a heavier bell.

**Short session note:** If feeling fatigued, reduce to 6 reps each side.

**LOAD:** Light bell (~20-30lb). **LEFT ARM FIRST — match the right to it.**
- **Upper arm pinned to the ribs**, elbow doesn't drift forward
- **Slow lower to a FULL stretch** — the bell loads the bottom where a dumbbell goes slack
- **Shoulder packed DOWN**, no shrug to start

🔥 Near-failure fine on the last set. Twice a week is the dose — this is frequency for the left arm, not intensity.

**Short session note:** If feeling fatigued, reduce to 6-8 reps each side.

sets.name: 🌀 Brutal Complex (@Asgooch) — 35, Short Session
sets.notes:
**LOAD: 35lb.** ~10-12 reps per move (each side where it alternates), circuit-style. Minimal rest between moves, ~45s between rounds (reduced for short session).

swing → ab-stance goblet squat (alternate wide/narrow) → alternating bent-over row → close-grip pushup on the bell handles.

**Short session target:** Two rounds is the goal; go to three only if feeling strong. **Stop a round when the hinge stops holding** — there's a bent-over row and loaded squats in here, and a broken hinge under fatigue is where this block would hurt you.

**Pace it by your own map:** the ab-stance squats and the close-grip pushups are the work; the swing and the row are the rest. Don't spend on the swings.

- **Close-grip pushup: hands on the bell handles, elbows TUCKED**, shoulders packed down, body in one line 🛑
- **Control the descent on the pushup** — the wobble is the training effect, and rushing throws it away
- **Stop a round when the hinge stops holding**, not when the clock says so. There's a bent-over row and loaded squats in here

**Short session note:** If feeling fatigued, reduce to one round and focus on perfect form on the squats and pushups.

sets.name: Cooldown (Hip + Adductor + QL Release)
sets.notes:
Give the QL the full beat — the complex loaded the hinge hard. Short session: keep the cooldown but reduce durations if needed.

**Short session note:** Reduce each stretch to 30s if feeling pressed for time.

exercises.notes: Adductors — the ab-stance squats worked them.
30s each side. Let the QL downshift after the hinge work.

tips: **Short session focus:** Prioritize form and completion over load or rounds. It's better to do less well than to push through fatigue.
**Left arm first on the curl.** Twice a week is the point.
If the complex leaves the QL tight, take the cooldown seriously.

**Sleep deprivation scale:** If you slept well, do the full short session. If you're tired, reduce rounds and reps as noted. If you're exhausted, do just the warmup, banded prep, one round of Outside Snatch Flow, and cooldown.
